clips.title: Sperling · Whole report
clips.method: The course letter array appears for 50 ms, then disappears. Whole report asks for all remembered letters. Letter choices come from the lecture; size, screen appearance and response window are illustrative.

clips.title: Sperling · Immediate partial report
clips.method: The 50 ms array is followed immediately by a 650 Hz middle-row tone. The letters do not remain visible or become highlighted. Tone synthesis is conventional Python waveform coding. Layout and tone envelope are illustrative.

clips.title: Sperling · Delayed partial report
clips.method: The same 50 ms array is followed by a one-second blank delay before the middle-row tone. The video does not simulate a fading retinal image. One second is the illustrated delay, not every condition in the study.

clips.title: Brown–Peterson · Letters and distraction
clips.method: Uses the course example F Z L and 45, followed by a three-second counting interval and recall. Participants count backwards aloud; this silent preview leaves that interval blank rather than displaying answers. Appearance and initial presentation duration are illustrative.

clips.title: Change detection · 4 squares
clips.method: A 100 ms sample is followed by a 900 ms blank interval and a two-second test. One square changes color. The layout is newly coded, not a recovered trial. No accuracy or capacity is measured.

clips.title: Change detection · 6 squares
clips.method: A 100 ms sample is followed by a 900 ms blank interval and a two-second test. One square changes color. The layout is newly coded, not a recovered trial. No accuracy or capacity is measured.

clips.title: Conrad (1964) · Visual letter sequence
clips.method: Six letters from the original ten-letter vocabulary appear serially every 750 ms, preceded by three ready spots. Sequence B C F M P X is an illustrative sequence, not a recovered experimental trial. Participants wrote their recall on paper; the final blank interval represents that response opportunity.

clips.title: Brooks · Remembering the F
clips.method: Memorize the F, then inspect the response sheet while mentally following its outline. The F is removed during the response period. Uses the lecture's inside/outside variant; not a claim to reproduce every detail of Brooks's original protocol. No pointer supplies answers.

clips.title: Shepard & Metzler (1971) · Shape pairs
clips.method: Three intact pairs cropped from the published Figure 1 reproduced in the course slide. Each pair stays still, as the original task required mental rotation, not watching rotating objects. Five-second viewing windows are illustrative; original response times varied.

clips.title: Vogel et al. (2005) · Ignore blue distractors
clips.method: A directional cue lasts 200 ms, the memory array 100 ms, retention 900 ms and test array two seconds. Attend to red rectangles on the cued side and ignore blue rectangles. Positions/orientations are illustrative, not a recovered trial or EEG recording.

clips.title: Metcalfe & Wiebe · Triangle problem
clips.method: Shows the supplied ten-dot puzzle, then an illustrative solution moving three dots. The solution sequence is a worked example, not a participant recording or a measurement of insight. The study's 15-second warmth-rating protocol is not reproduced.

clips.title: Metcalfe & Wiebe · Chain problem
clips.method: Shows the supplied chain-puzzle figure first, then models the solution: open all three links of one chain (3 × 2¢ = 6¢), use them to connect the other three chains into a closed loop (3 × 3¢ = 9¢), for exactly 15¢ total. This is an illustrative worked reconstruction, not a participant recording or a measured warmth-rating trace.

clips.title: Candle problem · Materials and support
clips.method: A candle, matches, tacks and box are shown, then the box is used as a wall support. This illustrates the supplied problem and solution, with flat code-drawn objects and illustrative movement. It is not a participant's actual solution trace.

clips.title: Maier · Two-string problem
clips.method: The strings hang too far apart to grasp together directly. Pliers are attached as a weight to one string and it swings toward the held string. Timing and reach geometry are illustrative. The swinging solution is distinguished from a recorded participant response.

clips.title: Luchins · Water-jug mental set
clips.method: Shows two classic A/B/C capacity sets and coded operations for B − A − 2C, then the simpler A − C alternative on the second set. Volumes are exact arithmetic; flat jug sizes and action timing are illustrative. This is a worked example, not the original full training sequence.

clips.title: Tower of Hanoi · Three-disk sequence
clips.method: A valid seven-move solution for three disks. Every move transfers only the top disk and never places a larger disk on a smaller disk. The sequence demonstrates the operators; it is not a participant's search trace.

clips.title: Mutilated checkerboard · Pairing constraint
clips.method: Starts with the 8×8 board, removes opposite corners of the same color, and lays example dominoes across adjacent squares. This shows the pairing constraint, not a complete tiling or a recorded think-aloud protocol.

clips.title: Denes-Raj & Epstein · Jellybean choice
clips.method: Two bowls contain exactly 1 red among 10 beans and 7 red among 100 beans. One red bean would win a dollar. No chosen bowl or winning outcome is fabricated. The flat layout and preview duration are illustrative.

clips.title: Wason · 2–4–6 rule discovery
clips.method: Starts with 2, 4, 6, then shows example proposed triples and feedback under the increasing-numbers rule. These proposals are teaching examples, not a particular participant's recorded responses. Original interaction involved writing triples and receiving experimenter feedback.

clips.title: Donders · Simple and choice response
clips.method: Shows the lecture's light/button teaching version of simple and choice reaction time. Lights appear; no reaction-time result or button response is invented. It is not a claim that this modern display is Donders's historical apparatus.

clips.title: Stroop · Ink-color naming
clips.method: Short congruent and incongruent color-word lists. Name the ink color while ignoring the word. Words/colors are newly coded examples. List layout and timing are illustrative, not the original 1935 test sheets.

clips.title: Visual search · Feature target
clips.method: Find a red vertical bar among blue vertical bars. Newly coded feature-search example; fixed display and viewing time are illustrative, not original trial data.

clips.title: Visual search · Conjunction target
clips.method: Find a red vertical bar among red horizontal and blue vertical bars. The target's features occur separately among distractors. No gaze path or search order is imposed.

clips.title: Posner · Valid and invalid cues
clips.method: Maintain central fixation while an arrow cues a location, then a target appears. One valid and one invalid example. Timings, arrow appearance and response windows are illustrative; no eye movement or reaction time is fabricated.

clips.title: Egly et al. · Object-based attention
clips.method: Two rectangles remain visible. A bracket cues one end; targets then appear at the cued end, the other end of that object, or an equally distant end of the other object. Cue, gap and response-window durations are illustrative; the key manipulation is equal distance within versus between objects.

clips.title: Treisman & Schmidt · Brief shapes and mask
clips.method: Recreates the lecture's two black digits and four colored shapes for 200 ms, followed by a deterministic random-dot mask. Participants report digits first, then shapes. No illusory response is drawn as though it appeared on screen.

clips.title: Apparent motion · Alternating lights
clips.method: Two stationary discs alternate, with brief blank gaps. No dot travels between the locations. Coded demonstration timing is illustrative rather than the exact CogLab configuration.

clips.title: Müller-Lyer · Equal shafts
clips.method: Equal-length shafts are shown with opposing fins, followed by shafts alone. The second interval reveals equal physical length. This is a geometry demonstration, not a replication of cultural-group measurements.

clips.title: Gestalt · Similarity grouping
clips.method: Dot positions remain fixed while colors change from uniform to alternating columns, making similarity-based grouping visible. Newly coded demonstration.

clips.title: Word superiority · Word, letter, nonword
clips.method: WORK, an isolated K, and ORWK are presented for 50 ms on separate trials, each followed by a mask and D/K alternatives at the tested position. Choices correspond to WORD/WORK and ORWD/ORWK. Sequence and mask texture are illustrative; no choice is made for the viewer.

clips.title: Winawer et al. · Blue matching
clips.method: One blue reference square is above two comparison squares, with an exact match on one side. Color values are illustrative and uncalibrated; this cannot reproduce a Russian color boundary or measure a language effect.

clips.title: Lexical decision · Word or nonword
clips.method: A real word and a pronounceable nonword appear on separate trials for lexical decisions. These are authored example items and illustrative timings, not recovered experimental trials.

clips.title: Tanenhaus · One apple
clips.method: Reuses the verified LING406 reconstruction of the same study. Correct final movement is to the box; appearance and movement timing are illustrative.

clips.title: Tanenhaus · Two apples
clips.method: Reuses the LING406 two-referent reconstruction, with the second apple on a napkin. The existing instruction recording is not the original experimenter's audio.

clips.title: Anstis & Cavanagh (2021), Movie 2: virtual Müller-Lyer illusion
clips.method: Original article supplementary recording, browser MP4 provided by PMC. Related research variant; not a recording of the CogLab session. Original attribution and CC BY 4.0 licensing are retained. Related variants, not exact CogLab sessions.

clips.title: van Lier, Hazenberg & Ekroll (2024), Video 1: apparent-motion color illusion
clips.method: Original article supplementary recording, browser MP4 provided by PMC. Related research variant; not a recording of the CogLab session. Original attribution and CC BY 4.0 licensing are retained. Related variants, not exact CogLab sessions.
